title: 例えば — “for example”
summary: 例えば introduces a concrete example of what was just said. It is placed before the example, which is usually a noun or a short phrase. Used in both spoken and written Japanese.

patterns.form: 名詞A、例えば 名詞B（や名詞C）

patterns.gloss: At the start of a sentence: For example, ～

body.p: The general category comes first and the example follows. 果物、例えばりんごやバナナ. Giving two items with や suggests there are more, not a full list.
It is written with the kanji 例えば or in hiragana たとえば; both are common. The more formal 例を挙げると has the same meaning.
A general statement can be vague, so a concrete example makes it clear. Because it follows the topic naturally, it is used when explaining, persuading or giving advice.

examples.ja: 果物（くだもの）、例（たと）えばりんごやバナナが好（す）きです。
examples.romaji: Kudamono, tatoeba ringo ya banana ga suki desu.
examples.tr: I like fruit, for example apples and bananas.

examples.ja: 運動（うんどう）、例（たと）えば水泳（すいえい）は体（からだ）にとてもいい。
examples.romaji: Undō, tatoeba suiei wa karada ni totemo ii.
examples.tr: Exercise, for example swimming, is very good for the body.

examples.ja: 甘（あま）いもの、例（たと）えばケーキやチョコレートは食（た）べすぎに注意（ちゅうい）しよう。
examples.romaji: Amai mono, tatoeba kēki ya chokorēto wa tabesugi ni chūi shiyō.
examples.tr: Be careful not to overeat sweets, for example cake or chocolate.

pitfalls: Do not confuse it with the verb 例える (to compare). As a noun-phrase connector, it is written 例えば.
The example must belong to the category before it. Do not give an unrelated item.
